question: on the old v1 stats api, how do i get more than 1000 results from a breakdown?
reference_answer: The limit parameter maxes out at 1000 (default 100). To get more, make the same request multiple times with the page parameter, starting at page=1 and then page=2 and so on, since page numbers start from 1, not 0.
key_facts: limit maximum is 1000
Use the page parameter for more results
Page numbers start from 1
answer: If you want to get more than 1000 results, you can make multiple requests and paginate the results by specifying the page parameter [1]. Importantly, the page numbers start from 1 not 0 [1].

**site_id**

Domain of your site on Plausible.

**property**

Which property to break down the stats by. Valid options are listed in the properties section above. Note that the `event:hostname` property is unsupported as a breakdown property at this stage.

See time periods. If not specified, it will default to `30d`.

Comma-separated list of metrics to show for each item in breakdown. See the list of available metrics above. If not specified, it will default to `visitors`.

Some metrics require a certain filter or breakdown property. For example `conversion_rate` can be queried with a filter on `event:goal` or in a breakdown by`event:goal`.

question: the Force Single Sign-On switch is greyed out for me, why can't I turn it on?
reference_answer: Enforcement is disabled until some conditions are met: at least one SSO domain must be verified, at least one user must have logged in through the identity provider, and all Owners must have 2FA enabled. Hover over the switch to see which one is missing.

evidence.title: Single Sign-On (SSO)
evidence.text:
While this step is not strictly necessary to use SSO, it's important for ensuring only members provisioned through identity provider have access to the team.

SSO enforcement can be enabled from **SSO Policy** section of SSO configuration.

There are conditions that have to be met before "Force Single Sign-On" can be enabled though.

- At least one SSO domain must be verified
- At least one user must have successfully logged in through identity provider
- All Owners must have 2FA enabled

Tip: What if not all Owners can enable 2FA at the time of setup?
It might happen in a team with multiple Owners that some of them might be away and not able to enable 2FA right away. One way to resolve this is temporarily changing their role to **Admin**. Once they are back, they can log in through identity provider, enable 2FA and ask to have their role changed back to **Owner**.

If any of those conditions are not met, the switch is disabled and the reason is outlined once you hover over it.

Disabled Force Single Sign-On switch explaining that all Owners must enable 2FA

Once all conditions are met and you enable enforcement, logging in through identity provider will be the only way to access the team.

Tip: Owners can still use standard login in case of emergency
Providing this fallback is important to provide a way to resolve issues with misconfigured or malfunctioning identity provider. Please note, however, that Owners must still log in at least once through identity provider in order to access the team with **Force Single Sign-On** enabled.

question: my shopify storefront is tracked fine but checkout and thank you page visits dont show up. why?
reference_answer: Shopify doesn't load your theme on the checkout and Thank you pages, so the theme snippet can't see them. You need to add a custom pixel in Shopify's Customer events, which tracks checkout pages and events like add to cart and purchase with revenue.
key_facts: Shopify doesn't load the theme on checkout and Thank you pages
Use a custom pixel in Customer events to track them
answer: Shopify does not load your theme snippet on checkout and Thank you pages, which is why they are not tracked by your theme snippet [1]. To track these pages, you must add a custom pixel in Shopify's Customer events [1][2]. If you have already added the pixel, ensure it is set to Connected in your Shopify settings [3]. Additionally, if you have set the Customer privacy settings to Permission: Required, the pixel will not load if a visitor declines the cookie banner [3].

citations.quote: Shopify doesn't load your theme on checkout and Thank you pages, so the theme snippet can't see them.
A custom pixel in Shopify's Customer events tracks checkout pages and Shopify's built-in shopping events (add to cart, checkout, purchase) with revenue.

evidence.title: Shopify ecommerce tracking
evidence.text:
Here's how to add Plausible Analytics to your Shopify store and track add to cart, checkout, purchases, revenue and more.

There are two parts:

1. **Your Plausible snippet in your theme** tracks your storefront: home, collection, product and cart pages.
2. **A custom pixel in Shopify's Customer events** tracks checkout pages and Shopify's built-in shopping events (add to cart, checkout, purchase) with revenue. Shopify doesn't load your theme on checkout and Thank you pages, so the theme snippet can't see them.

Note: Moving from Additional scripts or checkout.liquid?
Shopify has switched off Additional scripts and checkout.liquid customizations on the Thank you and Order status pages: on 28 August 2025 for Shopify Plus stores and on 26 August 2026 for all other plans. If you had Plausible code there, it no longer runs. Use the custom pixel below instead.

## Add the Plausible snippet to your theme

* In your Shopify admin, go to **Online Store → Themes**.
* Click the **⋯** button next to your current theme and choose **Edit code**.

Add Plausible to Shopify

* In the **Layout** folder, open **theme.liquid** and paste your Plausible snippet just before the closing `</head>` tag. Your snippet is in the **Site Installation** area of the **General** section in your site settings.
* Click **Save**.

## Add a Plausible custom pixel for checkout and shopping events

* In your Shopify admin, go to **Settings → Customer events**.

Shopify Settings

* Click **Add custom pixel** and name it, e.g. **Plausible**.
* Choose the **Customer privacy** settings (see below).
* Paste the code into the **Code** box: the setup block first, then the blocks for what you want to track.
* Click **Save**, then **Connect**.

evidence.title: Ecommerce revenue and attribution tracking
evidence.text: If you're using Shopify, you can track checkouts, purchases and revenue with a custom pixel in **Settings → Customer events**. No changes to your checkout or order status page are needed. See our Shopify guide.

evidence.title: Shopify ecommerce tracking
evidence.text:
1. Place a test order. Shopify's test payments work.
2. Your Plausible dashboard should show:
   * pageviews for `/checkouts/…/token/…`
   * one **Purchase** with the order total (once you've added the goal)
3. If nothing arrives from checkout, check that the pixel is **Connected** and review its **Customer privacy** settings. With **Permission: Required**, Shopify won't load the pixel if you decline the cookie banner.

evidence.title: Adding Plausible with Google Tag Manager
evidence.text:
Create a tag with the type **Initialization** and paste your script ID into the **Script ID** field.

Under **Triggering**, choose **All Pages** (Page View) so Plausible loads on every page.

If the Plausible snippet is already in your site's code, remove it when the tag goes live so pageviews aren't counted twice. Switching to GTM loses no data, as your stats belong to the site rather than the installation method.

That's all a basic installation needs. Save the tag, then test and publish your container.

### Optional measurements

The initialization tag also has options for enhanced measurements. Some are ticked by default. Untick the ones you don't need and tick the ones you want.

Optional settings in the Plausible initialization tag

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **File Downloads** | Automatically tracks file downloads |
| **Form Submissions** | Automatically tracks form submissions |
| **Outbound Links** | Automatically tracks clicks on outbound links |
| **Hash Based Routing** | Tracks page paths that use a `#` in the URL. See hash-based routing |
| **404 Tracking** | Tracks 404 error pages. Tick the box and enter the title of your site's 404 page |
| **Custom Props** | Attaches custom properties to pageviews. See Add custom properties |
| **Capture on Localhost** | Records events on localhost |
| **Logging** | Logs ignored events to the browser console with a warning |
| **Auto Capture Pageviews** | Sends pageviews automatically. If you untick it, the script loads but sends no pageviews until you send them yourself with another tag, for example one with a **Page View** trigger |
| **Custom File Download Types** | Replaces the default file extensions for file download tracking, so only the types you list are tracked |

evidence.text:
If you're already running Nginx as your main web server or reverse proxy, you can also configure it to proxy your analytics. Start by adjusting your configuration as shown in the next step.

Tip: Don't want to manage your own proxy? We can handle it for you
Our managed proxy lets you send analytics through your own domain name as a first-party connection. All you need to do is set up a CNAME record using the instructions we'll send you and update the snippet on your site. We'll take care of everything else. Contact us for details.

## Step 1: Get your snippet

In the **Site Installation** area of the **General** section in your site settings you can see
the snippet specific for your site. It will look similar to the following:

```html
<script async src="https://plausible.io/js/pa-XXXXX.js"></script>
<script>
  window.plausible=window.plausible||function(){(plausible.q=plausible.q||[]).push(arguments)},plausible.init=plausible.init||function(i){plausible.o=i||{}};
  plausible.init()
</script>
```

Your snippet will have a different script location than the example above. Look for the `https://plausible.io/js/pa-XXXXX.js` part in your snippet - that's the personalized location for your site's script. Mark it down for subsequent steps.

evidence.title: Building a white-label analytics integration
evidence.text:
By default, the Plausible script is a third-party request from your customer's domain to Plausible's servers. Ad blockers and privacy-focused browsers can block these requests, which means some traffic goes untracked.

Running a proxy routes the script and the event collection through your own domain as a first-party connection. Ad blockers do not typically block first-party scripts, so you collect more accurate data for your customers.

Two options:

**Self-managed proxy:** You configure a proxy on your infrastructure to forward requests to Plausible. This works at the platform level, so it applies automatically to every customer site you provision.

**Managed proxy:** Plausible handles the proxy for you. No setup or maintenance required on your end. Available on Enterprise plans.

See the proxy overview for setup guides across different hosting environments.

evidence.title: How the free trial works
evidence.text:
Every Plausible account starts with a free 30-day trial. During the trial you have access to all Business plan features and limits, so you can explore the full product before choosing a plan.

## No credit card, no automatic charges

We don't ask for a credit card when you register. There's no payment method on file, so we can't charge you. Your trial never converts into a paid subscription automatically.

This also means there's nothing to cancel. If you don't want to continue after the trial, you don't need to do anything.

## What happens when the trial ends

If you haven't subscribed by the end of the trial, your dashboard is locked. You can still log in to your account.

We don't keep your website analytics data indefinitely after your trial ends.

If you don't subscribe, we'll stop collecting new stats and eventually delete your dashboards and all their stats permanently. We'll email you before deletion so you have time to subscribe or export your stats.

After your trial ends, we keep recording stats for a few more days, and the email we send when the trial expires says how many. Recording stops at midnight UTC on the last of those days.

Automatic deletion removes your sites and stats, but your login stays until you delete your account.

Subscribe before deletion to unlock your dashboards and keep your historical stats. Deleted stats cannot be recovered.

## Delete your account at any time

You can delete your account with a few clicks at any point, during or after the trial. Go to **Account settings**, scroll to the **Danger zone** section and click **Delete Account**. This removes all your sites and collected stats.

To start a new 30-day trial, delete your account and sign up again with the same email.
